title: Generative AI and Agent Security
learning_outcomes: Explain generative AI and Agent Security and connect at least two of its listed subtopics.
Apply the central idea in generative AI and Agent Security to a small example or select a suitable approach for a stated scenario.
Identify an important assumption, failure mode, risk, or limitation and describe how it should be checked.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study generative AI and Agent Security within Responsible AI, Safety, Privacy, and Security. You will connect the syllabus topics below to a small, inspectable example and practice stating what the evidence does—and does not—support.
content.why_it_matters: Responsible AI is a lifecycle practice. Assess foreseeable harms, data handling, security boundaries, transparency needs, and routes for human accountability.

content_blocks.title: The central idea
content_blocks.text: Generative AI produces new text, images, audio, video, code, or other content from learned patterns and conditioning inputs. Outputs are candidate artifacts and need task-appropriate checks for accuracy, rights, privacy, and safety.

content_blocks.title: Syllabus topics covered in this lesson

items.title: Prompt injection
items.text: A prompt specifies the task, context, constraints, and expected response format. Compare prompts on the same representative examples and score outputs against a predefined rubric rather than selecting only favorable samples.

items.title: Untrusted document and web content
items.text: Untrusted document and web content is one of the concepts used to reason about generative ai and agent security. Define the inputs, assumptions, and intended result in this context, then test the idea on a small representative example and document where it may not apply.

items.title: Sensitive-data leakage
items.text: Leakage occurs when training or model selection uses information unavailable at the intended prediction time or information from evaluation data. It can produce deceptively strong offline results.

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: 1. Identify what generative ai and agent security takes as input and what result or decision it is intended to support. 2. Read the example before running it and predict the output. 3. Run the small example, compare actual and expected output, then change one input or assumption and repeat. 4. Record what the example demonstrates and what it does not demonstrate about a real system.

content_blocks.title: A practical way to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with the task definition and the inputs available. Make the expected behavior explicit, choose a simple reference point, and inspect both ordinary examples and cases where assumptions may fail. Responsible AI is a lifecycle practice. Assess foreseeable harms, data handling, security boundaries, transparency needs, and routes for human accountability.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: If the output differs, check indentation and spelling, confirm you saved the intended file, and compare each input value with the example. If the example runs as expected, do not infer that it proves a trained model works; this snippet is a deterministic teaching aid. Keep sensitive data out of tests.

content_blocks.title: Check before you trust a result
content_blocks.text: This is a small, deterministic teaching example—not a trained AI model or evidence of production performance. Run it with a local Python 3 interpreter; do not paste secrets or private data into experiments.

content_blocks.title: Recap and next step
content_blocks.text: Recap: Generative AI produces new text, images, audio, video, code, or other content from learned patterns and conditioning inputs. Outputs are candidate artifacts and need task-appropriate checks for accuracy, rights, privacy, and safety. Next, connect this lesson to its prerequisite or next lesson and carry the same habit forward: define success, test a representative case, inspect failures, and document limitations.

content.task: Try it yourself: complete a small risk review for generative ai and agent security. Identify affected people, plausible failure modes, evidence needed, preventative controls, a residual risk, and the owner who would review the control after a change.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain the core concept and accurately refer to the source syllabus topics.
Record a prediction and compare it with a reproducible result or a clearly stated manual trace.
Document at least one limitation, safety consideration, or evaluation requirement.
hints: Write down the inputs, expected output, and assumptions before changing the example.
Change only one input or condition and compare the results with your original prediction.
Ask whether the example covers realistic cases, important subgroups, and failure conditions; a toy example does not establish production reliability.
troubleshooting: Use Python 3 and run the file from the folder where it was saved.
If output differs, restore the original input and compare one changed value at a time.
If Python reports a syntax error, check copied quotation marks, indentation, and whether the full code block was copied.
These examples require no external packages, network access, model credentials, or personal data.
